input.text: Python list indices start at 0, so a list with n items has valid indices 0 through n-1. Your loop's range starts at 1, which means it iterates over indices 1, 2, ..., n-1 and never visits index 0. As a result, the first number in the input is left out of the total. To include every item, the range should begin at 0 rather than 1.

content.text: Python indexes lists starting at 0, not 1. Your loop starts at index 1, so it never adds the item at index 0 — that's why the first input value is missing from every sum.
